chapter: Tenor players, tours and band boys
title: Archie Bleyer's fussy studio and Business in F
summary: Bleyer moved the drummer around the studio for the right sound; Hinton played his Business in F as a teenager.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: I was just thinking about the first time that I recorded with Archie Blyer. Remember Archie Blyer?

I don't know, he had a thing -- he was very successful, you know that -- very successful; but you know, we used to go to do a session -- he was the only A&R man I know where you'd go to do a session and you'd spend two hours trying to find a spot where the sound was right, or where he thought the sound was right. I used to get so angry, because I used to have to move my drums every time he moved in to the studio, and we would start off in one corner, and end up in another corner, and before the session got started,

we were sitting in the middle of the floor someplace, and there was just a certain sound that he wanted, and he just kept you moving all over the studio until he got it. But all his records were successful.
That's right, he was a very meticulous man, and he had everything just the way he wanted it.
That's right. I often think of him -- I wonder what happened to him.
I haven't seen him -- he married one of the McGuire Sisters.
Oh yeah, that's right -- I recall that.

Yeah, and he's still in jazz and he's still a musician; I saw him at the Rainbow Grill once when I played up there, and I made an album -- the last time I was with Teddy Wilson, I worked with him -- it wasn't quite satisfactory to him, and I don't think he ever released it because he could afford not to -- if he wasn't quite satisfied. It certainly wasn't Teddy's playing.
Would you believe that before I met -- you know, it's a great thrill when you're a youngster and you hear about these people and you get a chance one day to have the opportunity to work with them.
Now Archie Blyer; I played his arrangement of "Business in F" when I was about 14 years old.
That's the first full beat arrangement I ever saw for the bass.
That's right. Then he wrote another
one called Business in Q. And I got the chance to work with him. It was a big thrill to me, you know?
